text:
Jackson LaCombe has 26 points in 25 games, and 25 of them are assists. At 25, he is playing 26:32 a night, up from 24:15 last season, and he is on the ice for 82% of Anaheim's power plays (65% last year). That is a breakout by any honest definition: from 0.71 points a game to 1.04, with 16 power-play points.

The catch is five on five. Anaheim takes just 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's out there, 10 points worse than when he sits, and he ranks near the bottom of the league in wins added because the goals haven't come (one, on 2.9 expected). Our numbers think his scoring rate is running above his talent too, with a range of 1.6 to 2.1 points per 60 against the 2.35 he's posting. None of that erases the playmaking: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 98th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey said Anaheim created chances at a high rate with him on. With the Ducks losing and Leo Carlsson hurt, how he handles even-strength minutes is the story to watch.
headline: LaCombe's breakout comes with a catch
